title: Taking stock of Africa’s economic transformation: rethinking sources of productivity growth
publisher: The World Bank Research Observer (advance article)
summary: Recent structural change in Africa has boosted growth, but overall labour productivity growth remains modest. Manufacturing has played a limited role since the 1990s, while services, especially wholesale and retail trade, have driven the gains.
keyFindings: Structural change has contributed to growth, but productivity growth remains modest.
Since the 1990s, services, especially wholesale and retail trade, have driven productivity gains more than manufacturing.
Weak productivity growth reflects constraints such as limited infrastructure, extreme poverty, poor health and inadequate education.
note: Published online April 2026; author order as listed on the journal page (alphabetical).
